Richmond Daily Dispatch (1860-65): the University of Richmond publishes the
whole run as one TEI download and has no public search API, so
dispatch_prepare downloads it once through the checked downloader and builds
a local SQLite FTS5 index. Tools: dispatch_prepare, dispatch_search,
dispatch_get_article, dispatch_issue. TEI is read with regular expressions
(it declares an external DTD), articles are numbered like the site's own ids
once ad-blank placeholders are dropped, and records are keyed by TEI file
because two issue dates in the source disagree with their titles.

Chronicling America, live API (chronam_search, chronam_get_page,
chronam_page_text): follows the loc.gov JSON API query shape recorded in the
Library's own notebooks. loc.gov limits clients to 20 requests a minute and
may show a bot challenge, so requests are paced at 3 s and a challenge or a
persistent 429 raises Blocked and starts a 10 minute cool-down for that
source only. doctor reports BLOCKED without failing.

Chronicling America, bulk OCR (chronam_bulk_plan, chronam_bulk_start,
chronam_bulk_status, chronam_local_search, chronam-index): for whole years,
streams the Library's per-batch .tar.bz2 archives and keeps only OCR text in
the requested date range in a local index. Archives are verified against the
published SHA-256; by default archives that start after the range are
skipped (range request of the first member) and reading stops once the range
has been passed, which leaves those archives unverified (--verify turns it
off). Planning is resumable and reports what it could not check.

Shared: Blocked error and per-source cool-down in http.py, date_range and
match_query in util, newspaper_page rights in rights.py.

Not included: Virginia Chronicle, whose OAI-PMH endpoints are behind a bot
challenge and whose robots.txt disallows crawlers.

Tests use real excerpts where possible (a trimmed TEI issue, a result record
from the Library's notebook, real batch manifest and title rows, real OCR
pages). The live API adapter has not run successfully against loc.gov from
the development machine; the bulk archive reader was run on a real archive.

- NARA's date filter also matches records whose parent series or file
  spans the range, so undated and out-of-range records come back; the

  misleading HTTP 200.
- Empty results with filters give a hint: geographic and creators match

  missing bytes or media means.

The adapter was written from the published spec with a hand-made fixture.
Run against a live key it needed these changes:

- rights: "Restricted - Possibly" and "Undetermined" are unknown, not
  restricted; NARA's own note and specific restrictions are kept
- dates: keep year-only precision and "ca."; NARA only applies a date
  filter when both bounds are sent in one format, so both are always
  sent as full dates and a lone start or end now works
- creators: read contributors (photographer, mapmaker) with their role
- places split from subjects; record group, series and a citation added
- files: classify by extension, drop the 1234 size placeholder, expose
  objectId so nara_extracted_text can be aimed at one scan
- nara_extracted_text returns machine OCR and partner transcriptions
  (otherExtractedText), labelled; include_extracted_text now returns
  excerpts instead of only a flag
- first search page returns record-group and material facets
- a bad key or a parenthesised query returns the website as HTTP 200;
  say that instead of "not JSON"
- JSON error bodies (NARA's 422 lists the accepted values) and cut-off
  HTML error pages (the Internet Archive outage page dumped base64) are
  summarised properly
- long files are capped at 25 shown media; downloads still reach all
- type_of_materials and level are validated locally with forgiving names
- tests run on trimmed live captures

Version 0.2.0.

ia_grep_text compared a plain phrase character for character, so
"twenty-five prisoners" found nothing in a book whose scan reads
"twenty-five  prisoners", and "picket post of twenty-one men" missed
"post  of  twenty-one". A zero-match answer reads as "not in the book" to a
model, which is wrong and expensive to discover.

A plain phrase now matches across runs of spaces, line breaks and a hyphen
split by a line break ("twenty- one"). It is still a literal match:
metacharacters stay literal and the words still have to be the phrase.
